projects.title: Deterministic Raft Consensus Simulator
projects.shortDescription: A discrete-event simulation engine for validating partition tolerance and leader election under asynchronous network jitter.
projects.fullDescription: Engineered an event-driven framework to model network partitions, message drops, and clock drift in Raft clusters. Designed deterministic replay capability to isolate Byzantine anomalies and race conditions in leader election cycles.
projects.contribution: [Formulated the state machine replication logic, implemented the discrete-event simulation queue, and constructed the network partition chaos harness.]
objectives: Verify Raft safety invariants across asymmetric multi-node network partitions.
Enable 100% deterministic replay of race conditions via seedable pseudo-random event scheduling.
Benchmark election timeout convergence under simulated 10ms–500ms packet latency.
projects.approach: Adopted a discrete-event clock decoupled from wall-clock time. Every RPC, socket timeout, and disk I/O step is modeled as an immutable event tuple dispatched through a priority queue.
projects.implementation: Core consensus logic implemented as a pure state transition function `(State, Event) -> (NewState, Actions)`. Side-effects (network emissions, timer resets) are returned explicitly as actions, allowing test harnesses to inject arbitrary partitions without mocking sockets.
challenges: Split-vote loops occurring when election timers clustered within narrow jitter bands.
State machine divergence during uncommitted log truncation after partition healing.
iterations: v0.1: Native multi-threaded simulation with POSIX timers (non-deterministic, difficult to reproduce).
v0.2: Virtual tick-based scheduler using priority queues (eliminated flaky tests).
v1.0: Added automated linearizability checker verifying client read/write log consistency.
projects.results: Simulated 100,000 partition scenarios across 5-node clusters with zero linearizability violations. Replay fidelity achieved exact bit-for-bit event reproduction.
projects.lessonsLearned: Pure state transitions separate algorithmic correctness from asynchronous execution mechanics, radically reducing concurrency bugs.

projects.title: Zero-Copy LSM Log Indexer
projects.shortDescription: A lightweight Log-Structured Merge (LSM) storage engine optimized for memory-bounded telemetry ingestion.
projects.fullDescription: Designed a specialized embedded log storage engine utilizing memory-mapped append logs, block-level Bloom filters, and tiered compaction to sustain high write throughput under tight RAM constraints.
projects.contribution: [Implemented the SkipList memtable, designed the SSTable binary layout with crc32 verification, and optimized the multi-threaded compaction worker.]
objectives: Achieve sustained write throughput exceeding 150k ops/sec on standard NVMe drives.
Bound memory footprint strictly within 256MB using arena allocators and tiered flushes.
Prevent write-stall spikes during background SSTable compaction cycles.
projects.approach: Employed Log-Structured Merge architecture with immutable memtables flushed sequentially. Reads pass through sparse index blocks and bit-vector Bloom filters to minimize disk seeks.
projects.implementation: Engineered lock-free SkipList memtable utilizing atomic pointer CAS swaps. Binary SSTable files are structured into 4KB data blocks, index blocks, and 10-bit/key Bloom filter footers with CRC32 integrity verification.
challenges: Compaction debt causing read amplification during prolonged burst ingestion.
Disk I/O contention between concurrent flushes and client write logs.
iterations: v1: Single background thread compaction (caused noticeable throughput drops).
v2: Dual-priority tiered compaction worker with rate-limited bandwidth throttling.
projects.results: Sustained 185,000 write ops/sec under 180MB RSS usage, maintaining p99 write latency under 1.2ms.
projects.lessonsLearned: Predictable memory allocation strategies and arena pools prevent allocator fragmentation in long-running storage daemons.

projects.title: Low-Latency Recurrent Audio Denoiser
projects.shortDescription: A causal hybrid CNN-GRU architecture for real-time speech enhancement on resource-constrained edge hardware.
projects.fullDescription: Developed a lightweight neural speech enhancement pipeline processing 16kHz audio in real time with under 15ms algorithmic latency. Evaluated across non-stationary background noise profiles.
projects.contribution: [Engineered dataset preprocessing, spectrogram STFT pipelines, implemented the causal GRU model, and quantized the network to INT8 for edge deployment.]
objectives: Deliver SNR improvement > 12 dB without introducing speech degradation.
Enforce strict causal processing with zero future-frame lookahead.
Execute inference within 8ms per 20ms audio frame on standard edge CPU.
projects.approach: Operated in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain using complex spectral mapping. Emphasized causal convolutions and recurrent memory cells to enforce real-time causality.
projects.implementation: Designed a U-Net encoder-decoder backbone paired with dual-layer bidirectional GRUs replaced by forward-only masked GRU cells. Applied perceptual loss (PESQ surrogate) combined with multi-resolution STFT loss.
challenges: Musical noise artifacts in high-frequency spectral bins under non-stationary noise.
Floating-point quantization accuracy degradation during 8-bit dynamic quantization.
iterations: Baseline: Standard time-domain Conv-TasNet (high memory overhead).
Refined: Complex spectrogram masking with post-filter phase estimation.
projects.results: Achieved PESQ score of 3.12 (vs 2.15 noisy baseline) with 12.8ms total latency and 1.8M parameter count.
projects.lessonsLearned: Loss function formulation directly dictates perceptual quality; spectral magnitude loss alone produces significant speech smearing.

projects.title: Visual-Inertial SLAM & Path Planner
projects.shortDescription: Monocular visual-inertial odometry and occupancy grid mapping for autonomous mobile robotics in GPS-denied environments.
projects.fullDescription: Constructed an integrated state estimation and graph-based SLAM system for terrestrial rovers. Combines Extended Kalman Filter sensor fusion with keyframe feature tracking and A* local trajectory generation.
projects.contribution: [Integrated IMU sensor driver fusion, implemented the loop-closure detection module via Bag of Visual Words, and tuned the local obstacle avoidance planner.]
objectives: Maintain drift rate below 1.5% of total traveled distance in indoor hallways.
Detect loop closures and perform pose-graph optimization within 100ms.
Navigate dynamic obstacle courses safely at 0.5 m/s.
projects.approach: Loosely-coupled visual-inertial fusion: ORB feature extraction tracks camera motion while 6-DOF IMU pre-integration constraints stabilize high-frequency rotational changes.
projects.implementation: ROS2 node architecture with separate threads for feature extraction, local mapping, and global pose graph optimization using g2o.
challenges: Feature loss in low-texture environments such as blank walls.
Sudden lighting transitions causing false-positive loop closures.
iterations: v1: Pure visual odometry without IMU (suffered scale drift and failure during rapid turns).
v2: Added pre-integrated IMU factors and keyframe culling strategy.
projects.results: Successfully mapped a 400m indoor test course with 1.1% cumulative position drift and verified obstacle avoidance at 0.6 m/s.
projects.lessonsLearned: Sensor synchronization timestamps require microsecond hardware triggers; software timestamping creates fatal Kalman filter lag.

projects.title: Capability-Based Microkernel Scheduler
projects.shortDescription: An experimental x86_64 priority preemptive scheduler enforcing hard memory isolation and capability security tokens.
projects.fullDescription: Researched operating system security models by authoring an educational bare-metal microkernel. Implements capability tokens for IPC endpoints, paging-enforced virtual memory isolation, and round-robin multi-level feedback queue scheduling.
projects.contribution: [Wrote the 64-bit bootloader transition, implemented the GDT/IDT hardware interrupt handlers, and coded the context-switch assembly routines.]
objectives: Implement a fully preemptive timer interrupt context switch without memory corruption.
Enforce strict user-space capability permissions for IPC message dispatch.
Support basic dynamic memory allocation via physical frame allocators.
projects.approach: Zero-dependency bare-metal kernel booted via Multiboot2. Enforces separation between privileged kernel supervisor mode and unprivileged ring 3 user tasks.
projects.implementation: Assembly interrupt dispatch table preserves register state onto the process kernel stack. The scheduler inspects runnable queues and swaps CR3 page tables before executing `iretq`.
challenges: Debugging silent triple-fault resets during paging initialization.
Stack misalignment triggering SSE exception faults in user-space code.
iterations: Step 1: Real-mode 16-bit to 32-bit protected mode jump.
Step 2: 4-level paging setup and long-mode (64-bit) activation.
Step 3: Preemptive APIC timer scheduler with 4 priority bands.
projects.results: Demonstrated stable preemption across 16 concurrent user tasks running isolated memory loops in QEMU.
projects.lessonsLearned: Hardware context switching requires meticulous ABI compliance; stack pointer alignment bugs can manifest as seemingly random CPU exceptions.
